newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - C&W cuts Veba tie, opens up strategy.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - C&W cuts Veba tie, opens up strategy.

text.p: British telecoms group Cable & Wireless Plc on Friday confirmed a widely-expected plan to leave its alliance with Germany's Veba AG, creating a clean sheet for its continental European strategy.

By selling out its 45 percent interest in the Vebacom GmbH mobile, cable and networks venture for 2.21 billion marks ($1.34 billion), C&W raised a war chest that it will use to cut debt and underpin its development plans across telecoms and cable TV.

In a statement describing the move, C&W said it expected the sale, adjusted for its parallel buyout of Veba's half of the much smaller Cable & Wireless Europe SA, would lead to enhanced earnings in the year ending March 31, 1998.
C&W also predicted a one-off pretax profit boost of 60 million pounds ($98.41 million) in the current financial year.
But, while utility group Veba has pledged to remain a shareholder in C&W, hanging on to a 10.4 percent stake, the British firm promised to press on with new European investments.

"Europe remains a key strategic market for Cable & Wireless, and the company will concentrate its efforts in continental Europe on developing business which will strengthen and support Cable & Wireless Communications' position," it said.
C&W Communications is a British-based venture formed last year to consolidate a number of companies' cable interests as well as bringing in C&W's Mercury mobile and networks business.
It has now been clearly identified as the platform for the group's expansion, but its growth prospects remain largely unknown.

Share analysts who have openly speculated about the strategy vacuum that could arise from the ending of the C&W/Veba relationship said on Friday they were reassured by their first impressions of the terms of the split.

Commenting on the profit boost that C&W predicted from the deal, Nikko Europe analyst Dennis Exton said, "that doesn't alter fundamental arguments, but it is something that should reassure investors."
"It's a fair get-out price. From C&W's point of view they couldn't have hoped for more," he added.
Exton said it was also a relief that Veba had agreed to notify C&W in advance of any plans to dispose of its shares in the British company.
"That's reassuring -- there won't be 10.4 percent of 2.2 billion shares hitting the market unannounced," he added.
C&W shares advanced in early trade, also greeting the moves positively, and stood up 10-1/2 pence at 486p by 0840 GMT.

Other analysts who anticipated the deal over recent days feared that unless C&W seals a deal with an international carrier such as Global One, which incorporates Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and America's Sprint Corp, its European aims could founder through weakness.

They said C&W alone would lack a cohesive set of mobile telephone investments in Europe and most felt that shunting voice and data down lines leased from dominant telecoms operators, who would then determine C&W's cost base, would not be the most effective way to enter markets.
